slide.title: Slides paint with tokens
slide.takeaway: Generated slides read the diagram tokens, so they follow light and dark mode and the reviewer's toggle; fixed-colour slides sit on paper in dark mode.

item.label: Colours are token references
item.description: Default styles, palette, canvas, markers, and tab and pin text name diagram tokens as @name, written as a light value plus an inline var(); the SVG declares them for both schemes. Authors may name any colour token.

item.label: Served visuals declare every token
item.description: Every SVG or HTML slide the reviewer serves gets a style declaring every token for the scheme its URL names, or both under prefers-color-scheme, validated by a digest of the bytes.

item.label: Frames follow the toggle
item.description: Slide frames and thumbnails are marked data-slide-visual; theme.js keeps their URLs naming the pinned scheme when it differs from the OS, through toggles, OS changes, and swaps.

item.label: Frames need the scheme in the URL
item.body: You might expect a frame element's color-scheme to set its prefers-color-scheme; only Firefox does. Chromium and WebKit follow the OS, so the URL names the scheme and the served style forces it.

item.label: Fixed-colour slides sit on paper
item.description: An SVG or HTML slide that neither switches on prefers-color-scheme nor reads a contract token, or an image, keeps a light frame on the slide-paper card in dark mode.

item.label: A one-time re-render
item.description: The renderer is change-saga-diagram/2; each re-renderable slide here was republished with an empty diagram edit, and SPEC explains the one-time re-render.

item.label: Tests
item.description: Goldens change only by added styles; tests cover token references, standalone dark declarations, served schemes, paper detection, and a Playwright toggle. visual-qa captures light and dark.
